#### What this PR does / why we need it:
During a scale down, we assume pods with missing metrics to be using 100% of the desired resource. However, it can happen that the target >= 100%
Eg.
```
type: Resource
resource:
  name: cpu
  target:
    type: Utilization
    averageUtilization: 200
```
Here 200% actually means 2 cores (cpu). Hence, during a case of a potential scale down, to compute the average more conservatively, we should consider the fallback as max(100%, resource utilization)

Background from [HPA docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/):

> If there were any missing metrics, the control plane recomputes the average more conservatively, assuming those pods were consuming 100% of the desired value in case of a scale down, and 0% in case of a scale up. This dampens the magnitude of any potential scale.

issue_context.title: Increase fallback consumption for HPAs with target over 100%
issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?

Change the fallback consumption from `100%` to `max(100%, target)` when pod metrics are missing on a scale down.

Background from [HPA docs](https://kubernetes.io/docs/tasks/run-application/horizontal-pod-autoscale/):
> If there were any missing metrics, the control plane recomputes the average more conservatively, assuming those pods were consuming 100% of the desired value in case of a scale down, and 0% in case of a scale up. This dampens the magnitude of any potential scale.

### Why is this needed?

The fallback value of 100% is supposed to be a safe overestimate of the desired value to dampen the magnitude of a potential scale down. However, if a metric target is set to more than 100% then this fallback typically becomes an **underestimate** that **amplifies** a potential scale down.

Note that a metric target of over 100% is a valid HPA configuration.

### Alternative fallback

We could choose a fallback of `max(100%, target + safety_margin)` instead. However, any safety margin would be arbitrary and I think it's better to opt for simplicity vs. precision in this corner case.
